headline: Council approves Lahaina Community Land Trust items, rejects Planning Commission nominee

meeting.summary: The council approved grant exceptions 8-0 and a managed retreat fund resolution 9-0 for the trust, and rejected a Maui Planning Commission nominee 5-4. Bill 26 on fire code fines went to committee for questions to the fire department.
meeting.recap: The council voted 8-0, with one member excused, to approve a group of board and commission appointments.[[2:40:06]] On a 5-4 roll call vote, the council rejected a nominee to the Maui Planning Commission.[[2:58:04]] The council voted 8-0, with one member excused, to approve grant exceptions for the Lahaina Community Land Trust.[[5:18:58]] A bill adding fire code fines was pulled and sent to committee for questions to the fire department.[[5:31:55]]
meeting.next: Council members will send their nominees' applications to the independent nominating board. Bill 26 on fire code fines goes to committee for questions to the fire department.

issues.oneLine: The council took up exceptions to county code conditions so the Lahaina Community Land Trust can receive a grant.
issues.why: The trust's director said the grants help Lahaina families fill their insurance gap and rebuild instead of selling their land.
issues.next: The trust said it was about to choose its first four insurance gap grant recipients.
issues.brief: The trust said it has secured two parcels and is under contract for four more, zoned for 13 permanently affordable homes.[[#1]] The trust said its pilot program has funding to support about 10 families.[[#2]] Under the grants, the trust gets first right of offer if a property ever sells.[[#3]] The council approved the exceptions 8-0, with one member excused.[[#4]]

issues.oneLine: The council took up a resolution to let the Lahaina Community Land Trust use the county's managed retreat fund to buy property.
issues.why: The trust's director said some Lahaina shoreline families may not be able to rebuild what they lost in the fire because of shoreline issues.
issues.brief: The trust asked to use up to five million dollars it was allocated from managed retreat funds for land acquisition.[[#1]] The trust said it talks with county and state staff to avoid spending county managed retreat money on land that state or federal funds could secure.[[#2]] The trust said it buys the land and gives the family resources to move inland.[[#3]] The council approved the resolution 9-0.[[#4]]
